object.title: Product Marginals, Density Bounds and Slow Spectra of Ising Transfer Kernels

method.scope: Finite-dimensional transfer spectra, including dimension-uniform bounds at fixed density cap and coupling; no physical mass gap or continuum theorem.

overall.aggregation: Unweighted arithmetic mean of five criteria; stars equal score divided by two.
overall.reason: Strong correctness and clear explicit proofs; originality and wider significance remain moderately supported rather than established.

correctness.reason: No substantive error found in all proof chains, including zero-density support and reverse-hypercontractive normalization; fallible analytical AI review, not formal verification.

clarity.reason: Precise operator definitions, constants and scope; dense abstract and sign-part proof need minor explanatory expansion.

originality.reason: Potentially useful joint synthesis and explicit density complement, based on classical methods; targeted literature check does not establish priority.

significance.reason: Useful separation of marginal information and relaxation in a specialized transfer family; no concrete fixed-range or physical application and no sharp quantitative theory demonstrated.

reproducibility.reason: Self-contained analytical proofs, explicit constants and object identities; build, rendered-image provenance and advertised full audit package not independently reproduced here.

recommendation: Suitable for transparently labelled working-paper deposit with this complete assessment and limitations. Deeper literature comparison and application positioning requested before a substantial-novelty journal claim. Not human peer review or editorial acceptance.

objections.text: Historical originality is not established. Compare exact hypotheses and conclusions with quantitative positivity-improving/hyperbounded-operator results and code-supported transfer/noise constructions before claiming major novelty.

Sharpness is unexplored: at B=1 the exact gap is 1-rho, but the bound is 2^(-2e_rho), severely weaker near rho=1. Include this benchmark and explain useful parameter regimes; Corollary 8 need not have a sharp exponent.

Global many-body weights and full-configuration transitions limit physical/local relevance. Supply a concrete application of the joint marginal obstruction within the stated class. No fixed-range Gibbs or continuum inference is justified.
Explain the pointwise sign-part inequality on and off each sign support and the integrated unit-norm step yielding <f,P_rho f> >= lambda_2. Current proof is valid but compressed.

This assessment did not rebuild the PDF, independently bind rendered images to that build, or inspect the advertised complete source audit package. Publish a manifest/build recipe; do not call this review successful build reproduction or machine proof.
Abstract and page 7 are dense. Add a short explanation of the sign-parts/cross-entry proof strategy. No visual clipping or broken references was found in the supplied pages.
